frozen.reason: Fresh function/version on the already tested traversal domain; no bank answer or manual program is proposal context.

scope.description: Input children may be null, undefined, booleans, strings, numbers (including NaN and signed zero), bigint, symbols, functions, finite acyclic arrays (including holes), or ordinary React element/fragment/portal data with scalar keys. Observe count or the complete forEach callback argument/index/receiver sequence, return identity and throws. Iterator/thenable/lazy protocols, library-read getters, nonprimitive key coercion, symbol keys, owner Fiber graphs, aliased callback arguments and input mutations require separate evidence. Unaccessed element warning descriptors remain opaque.

proposal.reason: Children.count returns 0 only for top-level null or undefined. Otherwise it counts leaf child slots as traversed by React's child walker: booleans, strings, numbers, nulls inside arrays, and React element/portal objects each count as 1; bigint, symbol, and function values count as 0; arrays recurse through all indices including holes as undefined. I left non-array non-element objects at a frontier because the scoped domain excludes iterator protocols, getters, and object-child throw formatting.

Repairs the prior proposal by frontiering when counting would read an element/portal own key through unsupported mechanisms. Arrays recurse through holes as undefined. Top-level null/undefined return 0; within traversal, null/undefined/booleans/strings/numbers each count as one child slot. Supported object children are only react.element/react.portal records whose own data key is absent, null/undefined, or a primitive scalar among string/number/bigint/boolean; accessor-backed key reads and symbol/nonprimitive key coercion now leave scope via frontier.

Repairs the prior proposal by matching React 18 Children.count behavior for additional supported non-counted child kinds: bigint, symbol, and function contribute 0 rather than leaving scope. Arrays recurse through holes as undefined, so holes count as 1. Null/undefined at top level return 0 via mapChildren short-circuit; inside traversal null/undefined/booleans/strings/numbers and valid element/portal records count as one slot. Non-array non-element objects remain frontiered because iterable/object-error behavior and getter-sensitive property access are outside the declared evidence.
